courses.title: Introductory Psychology
courses.description: Introduction to methods and statistics, biopsychology, learning, perception, memory, cognition, motivation, assessment, developmental, personality, clinical, and social psychology. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 100 or PSYC 101 and 102.

courses.title: Introduction to Biological and Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: Introduction to Methods and Statistics, Biopsychology, Learning, Perception, Memory, and Cognition. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 100 and PSYC 101.

courses.title: Introduction to Developmental, Social, Personality, and Clinical Psychology
courses.description: Introduction to methods and statistics, motivation, assessment, developmental, personality, clinical, and social psychology. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 100 and PSYC 102.

courses.title: Career Exploration using Psychology
courses.description: Critical application of psychological concepts to further personal growth. Methods and strategies for exploring careers as a process that unfolds across the lifespan.

courses.title: Contemporary Topics in Biological and Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: A focus on the interpretation of contemporary research in neuroscience, cognition, perception, memory, and learning.

courses.title: Contemporary Topics in Social, Developmental, Personality, and Clinical Psychology
courses.description: A focus on the interpretation of contemporary research in social, developmental, personality, and clinical psychology.

courses.title: Questioning Psychological Science in the Media
courses.description: Use basic principles of quantitative psychological research methods to critique psychological claims presented in the media and to translate psychological science to everyday life. Intended for non-psychology majors to prepare for upper level courses. Majors should take PSYC 217 instead.

courses.title: Research Methods
courses.description: Focus on various research methods used in psychology, with an emphasis on critical thinking and experimental design. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 217 or PSYC 277. Restricted to students in one of PSYC Major, BA COGS Major. Corequisite: Either (a) PSYC 100 or (b) all of PSYC 101 or PSYO_O 111, PSYC 102 or PSYO_O 121. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

coreq.text: Either (a) PSYC 100 or (b) all of PSYC 101 or PSYO_O 111, PSYC 102 or PSYO_O 121

courses.title: Analysis of Behavioural Data
courses.description: Use of inferential statistics in psychology and conceptual interpretation of data; experimental design (laboratory, field research methods); presentation of data analyses in reports. Credit will be granted for only one of: PSYC 218, PSYC 278, BIOL 300, COMM 291, ECON 325, ECON 327, EPSE 482, FRST 231, GEOG 374, KIN 371, POLI 380, SOCI 328, STAT 200, STAT 203. Restricted to students in one of PSYC Major, BA COGS Major. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277, PSYO_O 270. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Research Experience
courses.description: Applied research experience in an active psychology research lab. See Psychology Department website for application. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 101, PSYC 102. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Behavioural and Neuroscientific Research Methods
courses.description: Research methods used in the neurosciences. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 217 or PSYC 277. Restricted to students in one of NSCI Major, BSc COGS Major (Cognition and Brain stream). This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Analysis of Behavioural and Neuroscientific Data
courses.description: Statistical methods for use in the neurosciences. Credit will be granted for only one of: PSYC 218, PSYC 278, BIOL 300, COMM 291, ECON 325, ECON 327, EPSE 482, FRST 231, GEOG 374, KIN 371, POLI 380, SOCI 328, STAT 200, STAT 203. Restricted to students in one of NSCI Major, BSc COGS Major (Cognition and Brain stream). Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Introduction to Psychopathology and Clinical Science
courses.description: The definition, history, and scope of mental illness; emphasis on the psychological factors that control its origins, maintenance, and modification. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 227.

courses.title: Brain Dysfunction and Recovery
courses.description: Cognitive and behavioral impairments resulting from brain dysfunction. Focus on the efficacy of various intervention approaches. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102, and one of PSYC 216, PSYC 217, or 277. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 301 or NSCI 302. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Infancy
courses.description: Human cognition, perception, motor, social, emotional needs, brain development and their interactions from birth until the emergence of language. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102, and one of PSYC 216, PSYC 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Tests and Measurements
courses.description: Theory and practice of psychological measurement, statistical models for items and tests, assessment of test reliability and validity, factor analysis, scoring. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 218, PSYC 278.

courses.title: Personality Psychology
courses.description: Theory and research on individual differences in motivation, emotion, and social behaviour. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Principles of Animal Behaviour
courses.description: Behavioural neuroscience; behavioural genetics; social systems; mating and parental strategies; instinct and learning; evolution of human behaviour. Credit will be given for only one of BIOL 310 or PSYC 306. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Cultural Psychology
courses.description: Cultural influences on human thought and behaviour; interactions of culture and self; multicultural experiences; intercultural relations; methodological issues. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: Theory and research of individual social behaviour; social motivation; attitudes; group interaction; socialization; prejudice. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Cognitive Processes
courses.description: Contribution of cognitive processes to perception, attention, and memory; cognitive development, language, thinking, and creativity. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Psychology of Sport
courses.description: Psychological theory, research, and skills training related to sport performance, exercise motivation, and adherence. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 311 and KIN 150 and 231. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: History of Psychology
courses.description: The principal trends of psychological explanation and events in the history of psychology from the earliest times to the present. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to Psychology Major or Psychology Honours students.

courses.title: Health Psychology
courses.description: Health-related behaviours such as smoking and drug use; effects of stressful events on health; methods for coping with stress; impact of chronic illness on the family; social support systems. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Childhood and Adolescence
courses.description: Human development from the preschool period through adolescence. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Applied Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Applications of theories and research in developmental psychology to contemporary social issues; topics may include daycare, child abuse, divorce and remarriage, substance abuse, sexuality. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Psychology of Sex Differences
courses.description: Theory and research on gender development and the influence of sex and/or gender on cognition, emotion, motivation, social behaviour, and health. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102 and PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Adulthood and Aging
courses.description: Issues, theories, and psychological research regarding adulthood and the aging process. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Brain and Behavior (I)
courses.description: The neurobiological bases of behaviour (I); Neuroanatomy and neural communication, neuroscience research methods, brain processes involved in perception and movement. This course is strongly recommended for students who have taken PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, PSYC 217. Restricted to all Arts and Science students with second-year standing or higher, excluding those in the B.Sc. Neuroscience specializations. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 324, PSYC 304 or PSYC 370.

courses.title: Socialization: Media Content and Effects
courses.description: Examines human development in the context of the socializing role of media. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Forensic Psychology
courses.description: The application of psychological theory and research to legal issues and the criminal justice system. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Memory: Historical, Clinical and Cognitive Perspectives
courses.description: Classical and contemporary metaphors for memory and their impact on theory development. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Memory II
courses.description: Organic amnesia; remembering childhood events; the self and memory; and the problem of distinguishing genuine from simulated forgetting. Prerequisite: PSYC 333

courses.title: Gambling and Decision Making
courses.description: The psychology of gambling behaviour, with emphasis on relevant work from judgment and decision-making, the cognitive neuroscience of choice, and clinical perspectives on disordered gambling. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: The Psychology of Language I
courses.description: Psychological abilities underlying human language; language processing, lexical representation, and principles of online conversation; animal versus human communication. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: The Psychology of Language II
courses.description: Language and thought; deriving psychological principles from language universals; the psychology of literacy, dyslexia, multilingualism, and natural language processing. Prerequisite: PSYC 336

courses.title: Directed Studies in Psychology
courses.description: Directed investigation of a research problem, requiring a written report of the findings. Requires the supervising faculty member's permission. See the Department's website for more information. Restricted to Majors in Psychology or Cognitive Systems with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Brain and Behavior (II)
courses.description: The neurobiological bases of behaviour (II); neural mechanisms underlying sexual behavior, feeding, sleep, motivation, emotion, learning and memory, psychopathology. Restricted to all Arts and Science students with second-year standing or higher, excluding those in the B.Sc. Neuroscience specializations. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 344, PSYC 304 or PSYC 371. Prerequisite: PSYC 324.

courses.title: Honours Seminar I
courses.description: Orientation to psychological research, with special emphasis on ongoing research within the department; effective presentation of research findings, oral and written; critical evaluation of research. Requires a research project. Restricted to students in Honours Psychology. Prerequisite: All of PSYC 217 or PSYO_O 270, PSYC 218 or PSYO_ 271.

prereq.text: All of PSYC 217 or PSYO_O 270, PSYC 218 or PSYO_O 271

courses.title: Honours Seminar II
courses.description: Continuation of PSYC 349. Restricted to students in Honours Psychology. Prerequisite: PSYC 348.

courses.title: Psychological Aspects of Human Sexuality
courses.description: Human sexuality from a biopsychological, behavioural, and psychosocial perspective. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Evolutionary Psychology
courses.description: Theory and research on the evolution of the human mind, with emphasis on implications for cognition and behaviour in contemporary environments. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Advanced Research Methods in Behavioural Sciences
courses.description: Prepares students for graduate studies or other advanced behavioural research; experimental design and analytic techniques; laboratory with computer applications. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher and a cumulative average at or above 76%. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 218, PSYC 278, PSYO_O 271.

courses.title: Neuroscience of Motivation
courses.description: Experimental analysis of hunger, thirst, exploratory and curiosity behaviour, maternal and reproductive behaviour, fixed action patterns, and complex processes involved in social motivation with emphasis on the biological basis of motivation. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of NSCI 201, PSYC 304, PSYC 344, PSYC 370.

prereq.text: One of NSCI 201, PSYC 304, PSYC 344, PSYC 370

courses.title: Neuroscience of Simple Learning
courses.description: Introduction to basic theories of non-associative learning, classical and operant conditioning. Experimental findings from behavioural and biological analyses with animals and humans. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 304, PSYC 324, BIOL 361, NSCI 200.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 304, PSYC 324, BIOL 361, NSCI 200

courses.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: Current research into human brain systems underlying cognitive processes such as perception, attention, memory, and decision-making. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of PSYC 304, PSYC 309, PSYC 344, NSCI 201 or (b) COGS 200.

prereq.text: Either (a) one of PSYC 304, PSYC 309, PSYC 344, NSCI 201 or (b) COGS 200

courses.title: Sensory Systems
courses.description: Anatomy and physiology of the sensory pathways and their relation to perception. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 367, BIOL 372. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of PSYC 101, NSCI 201 or (b) COGS 200.

prereq.text: Either (a) one of PSYC 101, NSCI 201 or (b) COGS 200

courses.title: Perceptual Processing
courses.description: Perceptual phenomena and their underlying brain mechanisms. Prerequisite: PSYC 367

courses.title: Behavioural and Cognitive Neuroscience I
courses.description: Advanced methods and topics in behavioural and cognitive neuroscience. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher who are in the Neuroscience Major or Honours or in the Cognitive Systems Major programs. Credit will be granted for only one of i) PSYC 304, ii) PSYC 324 and 344, iii) PSYC 370 and 371, iv) BIOL 371, or v) BIOL 372. Prerequisite: One of NSCI 201, COGS 200.

courses.title: Behavioural and Cognitive Neuroscience II
courses.description: Neurodevelopment and neuroplasticity, the physiological bases of several motivated behaviours (sleep, sexual behaviour, hunger and eating, drugs and addiction), cognition, the stress response, and brain dysfunction and recovery. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher who are in the Neuroscience Major or Honours or in the Cognitive Systems Major programs. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 304 or PSYC 324 and 344 or PSYC 370 and 371. Prerequisite: PSYC 370.

courses.title: Directed Studies in Behavioural Neuroscience
courses.description: Directed investigation of an experimental problem in Behavioural Neuroscience requiring a written report of the findings. Requires the supervising faculty member's permission. See the Department's website for more information. Restricted to Majors in PSYC or COGS or NSCI with second-year standing or higher. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Cooperative Work Placement I
courses.description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in Summer Session after third year. Work term report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Psychology. Prerequisite: Co-op Workshops. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Cooperative Work Placement II
courses.description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in fourth year Winter Session, Term 1. Work term report required. Pass/Fail. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Psychology. Prerequisite: PSYC 398. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Clinical Psychology: A Health Profession
courses.description: Theory, research, practice, and professional issues in clinical psychology, including a practicum placement. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 400 and 401. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277, PSYC 300.

courses.title: Clinical Psychology
courses.description: Theoretical and research foundations of the processes of assessment and behaviour modification in clinical psychology. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 400 or PSYC 401. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Strongly recommended: PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and PSYC 300.

courses.title: Research in Psychological Disorders
courses.description: Focus on the cognitive, biological, and motivational underpinnings of psychological disorders. Topics include current research methods, controversies in the research literature, and directions for future research. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277, PSYC 300.

courses.title: Human Emotion
courses.description: Developmental, cognitive, and social psychological theories and research on human emotion. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

courses.title: Psychology of Religion
courses.description: Cognitive, emotional, and motivational underpinnings of religious behaviour; supernatural beliefs, magical thinking, ritual, sacrifice; religion's role in morality, prosociality, health, violence, and intergroup relations. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

courses.title: Cognition and Culture
courses.description: Cultural learning; cultural variation and universality in cognition and emotion; cognitive and emotional bases of cultural phenomena. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

courses.title: Research in Social Psychology
courses.description: Representative studies on social psychological topics; emphasis on the formulation of significant questions and the design and execution of relevant research. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

courses.title: Cognitive Neuropsychology
courses.description: The structure of the mind as revealed by brain injury, neurological illness, and surgical intervention. Topics include attention, memory, language, sense of self, topographic awareness, moral reasoning, emotion, theory of mind, and social awareness. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of PSYC 304, PSYC 309, PSYC 344, NSCI 201 or (b) COGS 200.

prereq.text: Either (a) one of PSYC 304, PSYC 309, PSYC 344, NSCI 201 or (b) COGS 200

courses.title: Cognitive Development
courses.description: The development of fundamental cognitive abilities from infancy through adulthood, including traditional approaches to cognitive development as well as new areas of current investigation. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 302, PSYC 315, PSYC 319, PSYC 322, PSYC 325.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 302, PSYC 315, PSYC 319, PSYC 322, PSYC 325

courses.title: Social and Personality Development
courses.description: Comprehensive overview of the psychological processes in the social and personality development of infants, children, and adolescents. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Strongly recommended: PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 302, PSYC 315, PSYC 319, PSYC 322, PSYC 325.

courses.title: Research in Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Advanced study of current research in a specific area of developmental psychology. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 302, PSYC 315, PSYC 319, PSYC 322, PSYC 325.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 302, PSYC 315, PSYC 319, PSYC 322, PSYC 325

courses.title: Applied Social Psychology
courses.description: The application of social psychological research and theory to the solution of social problems. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

courses.title: Special Topics in Psychology
courses.description: Intensive examination of selected topics and issues in psychology. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 218, PSYC 278.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 218, PSYC 278

courses.title: The Self-Concept
courses.description: Theory and research on the self: development, knowledge, motivation, emotions, presentation. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 305, PSYC 307, PSYC 308, PSYC 358

courses.title: Community Psychology
courses.description: The relationships between social contexts and wellbeing with a focus on the application of psychology to disadvantaged populations and community development. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 300, PSYC 308, PSYC 314; or (b) PSYC 319.

prereq.text: Either (a) one of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 300, PSYC 308, PSYC 314; or (b) PSYC 319

courses.title: Environmental Psychology
courses.description: Psychological theory and research on the interaction between organisms and the physical environment; emphasis on applications to the design and management of constructed and natural environments. Strongly recommended: PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 300, PSYC 308, PSYC 309, PSYC 314, PSYC 319. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Advanced Seminar in Psychology
courses.description: Investigation of an issue, topic, or phenomenon in psychology, focusing on research deeply within a subfield or integrating research across subfields. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277 and one of PSYC 218, PSYC 278. Consult Section Notes or the Psychology Department website for 300-level course(s) recommended for a specific offering.

See the Department's website for more information. Restricted to Majors in Psychology or Cognitive Systems, with third-year standing or higher.

courses.title: Honours Seminar III
courses.description: Students carry out a research project and report on its development during seminars. Discussion of research with emphasis on choice of problems, research design and data analysis. Restricted to students in Honours Psychology. Prerequisite: PSYC 349.

courses.title: Honours Seminar IV
courses.description: Continuation of PSYC 448. Restricted to students in Honours Psychology. Prerequisite: PSYC 448.

courses.title: Behavioural Neuroendocrinology
courses.description: Detailed examination of the interaction between hormones and neural control of reproductive and non-reproductive behaviours; emphasis on gonadal and adrenal hormone effects on learning and memory in the brain. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 304, PSYC 344, PSYC 371, BIOL 372.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 304, PSYC 344, PSYC 371, BIOL 372

courses.title: Neuroplasticity and Behaviour
courses.description: Experimental findings and theory documenting the plasticity of the brain and its relationship to behaviour: emphasis on gene regulation, neurogenesis and cell morphology changes in relation to learning and experience. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 304, PSYC 344, PSYC 371, BIOL 372.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 304, PSYC 344, PSYC 371, BIOL 372

courses.title: Drugs and Behavioural Neuroscience
courses.description: Introduction to neurochemical systems and functional neuroanatomy; animal models of human cognitive processes and mental disorders; neurochemical foundations and treatments for mental disorders. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 304, PSYC 344, PSYC 371, BIOL 372.

prereq.text: One of PSYC 304, PSYC 344, PSYC 371, BIOL 372

courses.title: Advanced Neuroscience of Motivation
courses.description: Neurobiological pathways mediating five core aspects of motivated behaviour: (1) affective decision making; (2) motivated drive; (3) goal-directed vs. habit-based behaviour; (4) learning from negative reinforcers; and (5) disorders of motivation. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 361, PSYC 365.

courses.title: Directed Studies in Behavioural Neuroscience
courses.description: Directed investigation of an experimental problem in Behavioural Neuroscience requiring a written report of the findings. Requires the supervising faculty member's permission. See the Department's website for more information. Restricted to Majors in PSYC or COGS or NSCI with third-year standing or higher. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
